question: A plan has five independent steps, each 90% likely to go right. What is the chance at least one goes wrong, in per cent?
answer: At least one goes wrong: 100 − 59 = 41 per cent
move: Work out the chance everything goes right, then look at what is left.
ask: Which plan of mine depends on many things going right, each of which feels nearly certain?
trap: Each step looks safe, so the whole plan feels safe.
hint: Find the chance that nothing goes wrong, then turn it over.
steps: 0.656 × 0.9 = 0.59, so all go right 59% of the time
At least one goes wrong: 100 − 59 = 41 per cent
reference: Feller, An Introduction to Probability Theory and Its Applications, Wiley, 1968
